conflict_synopsis.core_view: Own the post-FOMC USD tightening premium against AUD, the G10 USD pair that has not yet paid for Australian housing damage and delivered US policy.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Australian housing/labor confirmation plus a still-intact Fed tightening path while AUDUSD catches down to other USD pairs.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: US tightening bias withdrawn or Australian housing/labor re-acceleration restoring AUD relative-rate support.

remit: express macro views through USD spot whenever a defensible USD pair exists
stance_summary: USD is the clean benchmark: post-FOMC tightening bias plus broadening G10 tightening should be owned in USD spot, not in a cross. AUDUSD is the laggard USD pair—Australian housing is already breaking while AUD has not paid the USD premium already visible versus EUR, GBP, NZD and CAD.

catalysts: Further Australian housing, transaction, and labor prints confirming the tightening channel is still biting.
US inflation and Fed communication that keep the post-hike tightening bias intact rather than one-and-done.
Continued G10 tightening impulse (BoJ follow-through, BoE hawkish dissent/QT) that sustains the USD policy premium AUD has not paid.
AUDUSD catch-down toward the 1m USD moves already printed in EURUSD, GBPUSD, NZDUSD and USDCAD.
evidence_refs: rollup:August CPI keeps the Fed tightening bias intact
rollup:Australian housing downturn deepens under higher rates
rollup:BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through risk

expression_comparison.rationale: Dedicated USD-spot seat. The discrepancy is that AUDUSD has not repriced the delivered USD policy premium and the Australian housing/tightening-channel break; that lives in the USD pair. A rates sleeve (US outright duration or AU-US 2Y RV) owns yield levels that are already historically extreme and does not harvest the FX lag. A cross such as AUDCAD adds CAD oil, BoC energy-pass-through and stronger Canadian activity as second-order risk on an Australia-versus-USD view.

trade.invalidation: Thesis fails if AUDUSD resumes higher because US inflation/labor temperatures roll over and the Fed tightening bias is withdrawn, or if Australian housing and labor evidence reverse into a re-acceleration that restores RBA hawkish relative-rate support versus the US. Wrong-timing, not wrong-thesis, if global USD bid pauses but AU housing physicals and US policy bias remain intact.
trade.mispricing: AUDUSD still trades as if Australian financial-conditions damage and the delivered USD tightening premium were comparable to a flat 1m outcome. The pair remains statistically rich (5y 84th percentile) while US front-end yields have already repriced hard and other USD pairs have already moved. The 2Y sovereign differential only mildly favors AUD (about +26bp, carry ratio 0.049) so the FX lag is not explained by a large AUD carry cushion; it is unexplained residual USD-underpricing versus AUD.
principal_risks: FOMC was already >90% priced; buying USD solely on the hike is stale unless the path and the AUD lag remain the live gap.
AU 2Y 4.999% versus US 2Y 4.76% and AU 10Y 5.348% versus US 10Y 5.01% mean rate differentials do not independently favor short AUDUSD; a relative AU hawkish re-steepening would squeeze the short.
AUD commodity/terms-of-trade beta into the energy shock is not quantified here and can bid AUD independently of housing.
US consumer temperature 48.5 with weaker confidence is a USD-negative tail if it ends the Fed tightening bias.
Positioning/flow is unavailable; crowded USD-long or AUD-short ownership cannot be tested.
No executable broker prices; research/reference ECB fixes cannot be used as entries, targets or stops.
trade.thesis: FACT: The Fed delivered a 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00% after August CPI kept the tightening bias intact; rate futures had already assigned greater-than-90% odds to that 25bp step, so the decision itself is largely known information. FACT: US 2Y is 4.76% (1y z 2.84, +57bp over 1m) and US 10Y is 5.01%; the desk thesis is that BoJ’s hike to 1.25% and the BoE’s 6–3 hold with three hike votes broaden global tightening and that the energy shock is constraining the G10 easing impulse. FACT: Australian housing is showing the tightening channel in physical data—NSW stamp-duty receipts -24% y/y, transactions -18%, Sydney/Melbourne values more than 7% below peak—while AU labor 47.8 and activity 49.2 sit at or below the US analogs (labor 50.2, activity 49.92). FACT: AUDUSD research/reference fix 0.712 is still in the 84th 5y percentile (z 1.23) with a 1m return of only +0.20%, versus EURUSD -1.89%, GBPUSD -2.07%, NZDUSD -3.90% and USDCAD +1.74% over the same window. INFERENCE: The USD policy premium is being paid in other G10 USD pairs; AUD is the residual, so the clean USD-spot expression is short AUDUSD rather than chasing already-extended USDCAD or already-washed NZDUSD. INFERENCE: Cross-short AUDCAD (5y z 2.76, 99.96th percentile) mixes a valid AUD-rich observation with an implicit CAD long that imports oil, BoC energy-pass-through and Canada’s stronger activity (53.2) and consumer (52.5) temperatures—unnecessary second-order risk. UNKNOWN: Cot/positioning is unavailable; executable broker levels are not in the packet; NZ official yields are unavailable so NZD relative-rate RV cannot be completed; whether AUD’s commodity beta offsets housing stress is not identified in this freeze.
why_now: The FOMC hike is now realized, not just >90% priced, and August CPI left the Fed tightening bias intact—known decision, still-live path.
Last-24 desk thesis: BoJ 25bp to 1.25% and BoE 6–3 hold broaden tightening and keep term-rate pressure elevated even where domestic growth is softer; that is new transmission after the Fed print.
Australian housing physicals (stamp duty, volumes, home values) document the RBA tightening channel while AUDUSD has not sold off with the rest of the USD complex.
US 2Y +57bp over 1m versus AUDUSD +0.20% 1m is the live level-versus-change gap; 5d AUDUSD -0.73% is only the start of catch-down.
